transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-09
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Alice Johnson (Redwood AE), Marco Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Luminar CTO), Tom Reynolds (Head of Search), Sara Kim (PM), Luis Gomez (Infra)

Summary (auto): quick demo of hosted embeddings + reranking, walked through sample queries, discussed latency and security.

[00:00] Alice Johnson: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alice from Redwood, AE on the account. Marco here is our systems engineer, he'll run through the rerank flow and some sample notebooks.
[00:12] Marco Chen: hi all, uh, just to set context, Redwood's hosted embeddings endpoint returns 1536-d vectors by default for our open models, we also support multiscale and custom dims, but for search we recommend the default.
[00:30] Tom Reynolds: quick question, when you say default, you mean the red — redwood default model? sorry, model names sometimes get jumbled in notes.
[00:38] Marco Chen: yeah, sorry, we have a couple of verified models; for embeddings we usually demo with rdx-embed-1, but the API accepts any model in the catalog.
[00:50] Priya Patel: can you walk through the reranking endpoint, like how it integrates with our current vector store? we're on an in-house FAISS cluster behind a sharded service.
[01:05] Marco Chen: absolutely. typical pattern: you do approximate nearest neighbor on your FAISS to pull top-K candidates, then call Redwood's /rerank endpoint with the query + candidate docs. Our rerank runs a cross-encoder style score and returns re-ordered results with confidence scores. latency wise for K=10 on hosted we usually see 40-120ms depending on model and batch size.
[01:28] Tom Reynolds: 40 to 120ms, that range is quite wide — what's the median and p95 for the hosted setup?
[01:36] Marco Chen: median is around 60ms for rdx-rank-small, p95 ~110ms in our US region under normal load; for large models it's more like median 120ms. Those are from our verified perf profiles but obviously depends on token length and doc size.
[01:52] Sara Kim: are you doing any batching on the rerank side? our queries are bursty throughout the day.
[01:59] Marco Chen: yes, the hosted runtime does micro-batching, but rerank cross-encoders are less amenable to big batches because of latency SLOs. We can batch small groups (2-8) with sub-10ms queuing; Optimize can suggest batch windows.
[02:20] Priya Patel: security: we need SOC2, SSO, and customer-managed keys (KMS) for embeddings at rest, plus audit logs retention for 12 months. Do you support that on hosted?
[02:34] Alice Johnson: short answer: yes for SOC2 and SSO/SAML enterprise, KMS for Private and Dedicated today, hosted can support bring-your-own-key with our enterprise plan — i'll include details in the security packet. Audit logs are available with the enterprise observability add-on.
[02:55] Luis Gomez: if we start with hosted but need strict residency, can we do a region pin or VPC peering?
[03:02] Marco Chen: yes region pinning is supported, you can choose region control; VPC peering and Private deployment are options if you need tighter network controls. For peering we have docs and a networking checklist.
[03:18] Tom Reynolds: on rerank results, can we get token-level attributions or highlights for why a doc was bumped?
[03:25] Marco Chen: we return score deltas and top contributing spans if you enable explainability in the rerank API — it's not super granular token attribution but span-level highlights are supported. There's a small latency overhead when enabled.
[03:40] Sara Kim: what's the expected cost delta if we add a rerank cross-encoder step on top of ANN?
[03:46] Alice Johnson: cost is typically per-rerank-call + embedding storage costs. For typical e-commerce scale, customers see a ~20-40% increase in token/compute spend per query but relevance lift often reduces downstream support/return costs. We'll estimate for your qps once we get sample logs.
[04:05] Priya Patel: we'd like to run an apples-to-apples eval: you run our 10k queries against our candidate set, measure MRR/NDCG before and after rerank. Can Redwood host the rerank eval or do we run locally?
[04:20] Marco Chen: we can do both. we have a benchmark template (notebook) we send to customers; if you provide data we can run it in a scoped pilot on hosted. If data residency is an issue, we can give you the notebook to run locally and walk through results.
[04:36] Tom Reynolds: what's the onboarding timeline for a pilot? we want to move quickly, maybe two weeks.
[04:42] Alice Johnson: typical pilot is 2-4 weeks: week 1 onboarding + data handoff, week 2 run benchmarks and tune, week 3 iterate. we can compress to two weeks if you prioritize.
[04:55] Luis Gomez: network-wise, we need support for SAML, SCIM and our audit pipeline to pull logs. does Redwood expose structured logs or push to our SIEM?
[05:05] Marco Chen: Structured audit events can be exported to your SIEM via our secure log sink (S3 or syslog). We'll include the log schema doc.
[05:14] Tom Reynolds: any concerns about hallucination with reranking? we rely on document snippets and retriever scores.
[05:20] Marco Chen: rerank is purely scoring candidates — it doesn't hallucinate by design because it's not generating content, it's re-scoring. If you use generation-based rerank you'll want guardrails; we recommend extractive spans for explainability.
[05:34] Priya Patel: demo time?
[05:36] Marco Chen: cool, i'll share my screen — walking through the notebook.
[05:42] [screen share noises, brief pause]
[05:55] Marco Chen: running a query: step 1 call /embeddings to embed the query, step 2 ANN recall from FAISS, step 3 call /rerank with the query and candidate snippets — here's the curl example, you can see payload shape: {"query": "...", "candidates": [ {"id":"doc1","text":"..."}, ... ] } and we return scores.
[06:18] Marco Chen: note: transcription sometimes mangles JSON braces, but the actual notebook has full examples.
[06:30] Sara Kim: how do you handle long docs? we have product pages with 3-4k tokens.
[06:36] Marco Chen: we chunk documents into passages; embedding store is passage-level; for rerank we can send top passages or include doc-level aggregator. Recommend 500-token passages by default.
[06:50] Tom Reynolds: for the benchmark, what's the metric set you recommend? we use MRR and CTR, but open to nDCG.
[06:57] Marco Chen: MRR, nDCG@10, and precision@k are standard; we'll include code to compute them in the notebook.
[07:05] Priya Patel: are there SLA options for hosted? our product needs 99.9 uptime and 50ms p95 for production ranking.
[07:14] Alice Johnson: hosted SLA is available on enterprise with performance commitments; if you need strict 50ms p95 we might recommend Dedicated or Private to get closer to that target depending on qps. We'll scope it during the technical deep dive.
[07:30] Luis Gomez: curious about cold-start tokenization and kv cache behavior for rerank/generation.
[07:36] Marco Chen: for rerank we don't use kv cache, that's more relevant for generation/streaming. For embeddings and rerank it's straightforward (stateless calls), so no KV cache considerations.
[07:47] Sara Kim: any rate limits we should plan for?
[07:50] Alice Johnson: hosted has burst and steady rate limits we can configure on the enterprise tier; we'll include recommended quotas based on your qps.
[07:58] Tom Reynolds: ok last quick thing — latency profiling. can you share a perf sheet or do we run A/B with our traffic?
[08:06] Marco Chen: we have a verified perf profile sheet per model and region, i'll share that. For your traffic we can run a small A/B in pilot and capture p50/p95 numbers.
[08:16] Alice Johnson: great, recap and next steps — i'll send pricing and contractual items, marco will send demo notebook and benchmark template, priya will share dataset and success criteria. we'll aim to kick off pilot next week.
[08:30] Priya Patel: thanks everyone, that sounds good.
[08:33] Tom Reynolds: appreciate the walkthrough.
[08:35] Alice Johnson: thanks all.

End of transcript.
